memory_leads.lead: The ship agent is a local representative/coordinator for a principal such as owner, operator or charterer, connecting the master and remote commercial/operations team with port authority, terminal, border/health authorities and local service providers; agency responsibility should not be collapsed into the authority of those separate actors.

Pre-arrival notification and document preparation form a readiness stage before the vessel reaches the port. ETA changes, voyage data, crew/cargo particulars and port-specific submissions can require repeated updates, making administrative readiness dynamic rather than a one-time form.
Inward clearance and outward/departure clearance are distinct states: permission/readiness to enter or begin a port call does not imply that all formalities needed to sail are already complete.

Customs interfaces can concern the vessel, ship's stores, cargo-related declarations and arriving spares or supplies. The structural memory is that customs readiness can gate port-call tasks even when cargo handling and nautical access are physically available; exact legal scope is deferred.

Immigration or border-control readiness is a separate crew/personnel state. Crew lists, travel documents and permissions can affect shore leave, joining/leaving crew and departure without changing the ship's mechanical readiness.

Quarantine, health or free-pratique-type readiness is another distinct interface between ship and port. Health declarations or inspections can condition contact, boarding or operations, while exact terminology and rules vary by jurisdiction and period.

Crew change is an end-to-end logistics chain rather than a simple personnel swap: relief crew travel, visas/entry permission, local transport or launch access, timing with the ship's stay, handover and repatriation all have to align.

Ship chandlers and provisioning services support food, consumables and routine stores during a call. Delivery readiness depends on ordering, local availability, access to the vessel and any relevant clearance, so husbandry consumes port-call time and coordination bandwidth.

Urgent spare parts can follow a separate courier/freight, customs-release, local-delivery and vessel-access chain. A technically diagnosed repair may therefore remain incomplete because the part has not crossed the administrative and physical handoffs needed to reach the ship.

Husbandry coordination can encompass fresh water, waste/sludge removal, laundry, medical support, launches, transport and other non-cargo services. The useful category is the bundle of time-sensitive support tasks, not an exhaustive service catalog.

Agency disbursement accounts or analogous port-call cost statements aggregate local charges and service payments for a principal; prefunding, estimates and later settlement create a financial-administration state separate from whether each physical service was performed.

Cash-to-master or other local vessel cash/expense arrangements are remembered as a husbandry-finance interface in some operating contexts, but exact practices, controls and jurisdictions are too variable for blind factual claims.

Cargo completion and even marine departure readiness do not necessarily equal sailing readiness: outstanding outward clearance, crew formalities, documents, inspections or essential husbandry can keep the vessel alongside or delay departure.

P022 physical port-call readiness and P023 administrative/husbandry readiness should be modeled as parallel state chains that converge at operational milestones; treating either one as a proxy for the whole port call hides why a nominally available berth or ready ship still waits.

The P010 crewing pipeline continues through the port interface: having a qualified relief seafarer available globally is not enough if travel, border, local transfer and vessel timing do not align for the actual crew change.

Maintenance readiness is partly a supply-chain state: spare-part ordering and delivery can couple shore logistics and clearance timing to onboard repair completion, extending off-hire or schedule impact without changing the underlying defect.

Port-call documentation has a strong known-time/revision dimension: ETA, crew, cargo or operational changes can trigger updated submissions, so replay should preserve what documents/statuses were known or accepted at each stage rather than assume the final package existed from the start.
The ship agent's broad role as local operational coordinator was introduced in P022; P023 retains only the administrative, border/health and husbandry dimensions of that role.

Cargo and inland customs/release handoffs can overlap P020's inland execution chain; P023 is limited to vessel/port-call clearance and support readiness rather than reopening cargo-delivery procedures.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Requirements differ materially by jurisdiction, vessel/cargo type and period; structural vocabulary is retained but exact law, form, notice and fee claims require Evidence.
Crew-change rules are highly jurisdiction- and date-specific and cannot be safely generalized from blind memory.
No reliable blind basis exists for exhaustive provider histories, ownership lineages or rankings across ports.
Event chronology, attribution and consequences require dated claim-scoped Evidence.

stop_reason: The local administrative/support port-call chain is populated from pre-arrival preparation through inward clearance, border/health interfaces, crew change, stores/spares and husbandry to outward clearance. Further recall becomes jurisdiction-, form-, fee-, provider- or incident-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation; no clearance rule, customs/immigration/quarantine requirement, visa/health condition, agency fee/account, service-provider identity or historical port-call incident is verified.
